facts.fact: Ghana's Data Protection Commission issued a statement on 20 October 2026 saying the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Parliament are registered data controllers in good standing with it, and that it will review the disclosure of evacuees' data.
The Data Protection Commission cited the Data Protection Act, 2012 (Act 843), sections 18 to 20, as binding obligations on the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Parliament.
The Data Protection Commission issued a public statement through its Public Affairs Unit on 20 October 2026 and said it will take regulatory action under Act 843 where non-compliance is found.

The Data Protection Commission publicly warned the Minority Caucus, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Joy News and other media over disclosure of personal data of some of 1,964 evacuees from South Africa, and said it would open a regulatory review.
The Data Protection Commission cited the Data Protection Act, 2012 (Act 843) as the law the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Parliament must continue to meet.
The Data Protection Commission is acting: it issued a statement on 20 October 2026 and keeps a register of data controllers.

The Data Protection Commission issued a public warning with protective measures on 20 October 2026 and announced a regulatory review of the disclosures; no decision against a named organisation is reported.

GHA.note: No criticism of a named government policy, cut or punishment is stated.
